description: More refuelling points: new stations or mobile units so daily queue time halves
lead_agency: Pi-CNG, with NMDPRA (licensing) and Lagos State / IBILE (IOGC)
lead_agency_basis: Pi-CNG plans to expand refuelling networks (S08); Lagos State's IBILE network (S37); 81 new retail licences (S10); NMDPRA is the regulator that granted NIPCO its regulatory approvals (S38).
impact_rationale: [Simulated] P(CNG pays) 91.5% vs baseline 61.8% (+29.7 pts; 10,000 draws, seed 42). Score from the fixed bands in policy_options.impact_score (>=30 pts = 5, 15-30 = 4, 5-15 = 3, 1-5 = 2, <1 = 1).
cost_rationale: [Judgement] High. New sites need land, compressors and a gas supply. Public money is already involved: the Ojota mother station and the 15-station IBILE network are MDGIF-supported (S37), and 1,000 stations have been ordered (S09). 81 new licensed retailers (S10) suggests private capital can share the cost. No sourced naira cost per station, so none is given.
speed_rationale: [Judgement] Slow. Four NNPC mobile units planned for end Jan 2025 are still unconfirmed (S35; lagos_cng_stations.csv), and the IBILE network was only commissioned in May 2026 (S37).
feasibility_rationale: [Judgement] Moderate. Depends on gas supply reaching new sites. Delhi needed a larger gas allocation as well as more stations (S28). Interest from retailers is shown by 81 new licences (S10).
evidence_rationale: [Judgement] Fairly strong. Delhi cut queues by growing stations from 30 to 112 alongside more gas (S28, H). 10 of 12 surveyed petrol drivers cite no nearby station (S47). Queue time is the input that moves net benefit most (notebook 06).

description: More capacity at existing stations: compressors, dispensers or opening hours so no daily queue exceeds 1 hour
lead_agency: Station operators (NNPC Retail / NIPCO, IBILE), supported by Pi-CNG and MDGIF
lead_agency_basis: Operators of the confirmed and commissioned Lagos sites (S34-S37); MDGIF supports CNG infrastructure (S37). Pi-CNG's role is judgement.
impact_rationale: [Simulated] P(CNG pays) 98.2% vs baseline 61.8% (+36.4 pts; 10,000 draws, seed 42). Score from the fixed bands in policy_options.impact_score (>=30 pts = 5, 15-30 = 4, 5-15 = 3, 1-5 = 2, <1 = 1).
cost_rationale: [Judgement] Medium. Uses sites that already have land and a gas connection, so likely cheaper per unit of queue reduction than new sites. Still needs equipment, and possibly more gas from mother stations such as Ojota (96,000 scm/day, S37). No sourced naira figure.
speed_rationale: [Judgement] Fairly fast. Equipment can be added at existing sites, and NNPC deployed mobile refuelling units at short notice in Lagos (S35, S36).
feasibility_rationale: [Judgement] Moderate. Capacity is limited by gas supply as well as equipment. Delhi's early queues came with a 32% supply deficit (S27, H). A 1-hour cap everywhere is a target, not something operators can guarantee.
evidence_rationale: [Judgement] Medium. The model and survey show queue time drives the result (S47; notebook 06), but there is no direct evidence on how much extra capacity cuts queues at Lagos sites.

description: Free conversion: government pays for the kit and installation
lead_agency_basis: Pi-CNG runs the free-kit programme and approved centres (S17, S39) and the 100,000 Conversion Kit Programme (S08).
impact_rationale: [Simulated] P(CNG pays) 65.5% vs baseline 61.8% (+3.8 pts; 10,000 draws, seed 42). Score from the fixed bands in policy_options.impact_score (>=30 pts = 5, 15-30 = 4, 5-15 = 3, 1-5 = 2, <1 = 1).
cost_rationale: [Calculated] High. 100,000 car conversions x NGN 1,300,000 (conversion_cost car mid, S40) = NGN 130 bn. Lower if many are keke kits (keke mid NGN 375,000; Low confidence). Pi-CNG already has a 100,000 Conversion Kit Programme (S08).
speed_rationale: [Judgement] Fairly fast. Approved centres already exist (6 in Lagos, S39) and a conversion takes 1-3 days (S40). Kit supply is a constraint: 93,845 kits deployed to date (S01, self-reported).
feasibility_rationale: [Judgement] Feasible. Already being done for commercial vehicles via associations (S17), so the machinery exists; the limit is budget.
evidence_rationale: [Judgement] Medium. 11 of 12 surveyed petrol drivers say they would convert if it were free (S47, stated intention), and 12 of 13 CNG users converted free. But uptake remains well below the 1m target despite free kits (S03, S07; conflict C2).

description: Cheaper loans: conversion loans at 5% a year instead of 15-20%
lead_agency_basis: MOFI and CREDICORP run the CNG conversion credit scheme (S18).
impact_rationale: [Simulated] P(CNG pays) 62.3% vs baseline 61.8% (+0.5 pts; 10,000 draws, seed 42). Score from the fixed bands in policy_options.impact_score (>=30 pts = 5, 15-30 = 4, 5-15 = 3, 1-5 = 2, <1 = 1).
cost_rationale: [Calculated + judgement] Medium. Interest given up on one NGN 1.3m car loan over 2 years at 5% instead of 17.5%: about NGN 181,317 (S40, S18; policy_options.interest_subsidy_per_loan), so about NGN 18 bn per 100,000 loans. The scheme is NGN 10 bn with NGN 2.5 bn seed (S18). The Medium rating is judgement.
speed_rationale: [Judgement] Fairly fast. Changes the rate on an existing scheme (S18) rather than building something new.
feasibility_rationale: [Judgement] Feasible. Existing institutions and scheme (S18). Needs funding for the interest gap.
evidence_rationale: [Judgement] Weak. No evidence on how many drivers have taken up the scheme. In the model, the loan is small next to fuel savings and queue costs, so the rate barely matters (notebook 06).

description: Stable CNG price: hold the pump price at the mid value instead of letting it vary
lead_agency_basis: Judgement: NMDPRA regulates the downstream sector; NADDC announced the official NGN 380/scm rate (S10).
impact_rationale: [Simulated] P(CNG pays) 61.5% vs baseline 61.8% (-0.2 pts; 10,000 draws, seed 42). Score from the fixed bands in policy_options.impact_score (>=30 pts = 5, 15-30 = 4, 5-15 = 3, 1-5 = 2, <1 = 1).
cost_rationale: [Judgement] Medium, uncertain. A published price band or agreement could cost little, but holding the price below market would need a subsidy whose size depends on gas costs. No sourced figure.
speed_rationale: [Judgement] Moderate. A regulatory decision, but it needs agreement from operators.
feasibility_rationale: [Judgement] Hard. Prices have moved by station and overnight (S12, S13), and capping prices risks operators selling less or closing.
evidence_rationale: [Judgement] Weak. Price shocks are documented (S12), but the model shows no gain on average. Any benefit is predictability for drivers, which the model does not capture.
